statement: reconstruct_queue(people) returns a result r (it does not fail) such that: (a) len(r) = n and for every j with 0 <= j < n, len(r[j]) = 2; (b) there is a bijection sigma : {0,...,n-1} -> {0,...,n-1} such that for every j with 0 <= j < n, r[j][0] = people[sigma(j)][0] and r[j][1] = people[sigma(j)][1]; (c) for every j with 0 <= j < n, if h = r[j][0] and k = r[j][1], then the number of indices i with 0 <= i < j and r[i][0] >= h is exactly k.
preconditions: Let n = len(people). Assume: 1 <= n <= 2000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(people[i]) = 2; writing people[i] = [h_i, k_i], 0 <= h_i <= 10^6 and 0 <= k_i < n; and there is a bijection pi : {0,...,n-1} -> {0,...,n-1} such that, setting q[j] = people[pi(j)] for 0 <= j < n, for every j the number of i with 0 <= i < j and q[i][0] >= q[j][0] equals q[j][1].

statement: reconstruct_queue(people) returns a result r; in particular it does not return an error, panic, or overflow.

statement: reconstruct_queue(people) returns a result r such that len(r) = n, every r[j] for 0 <= j < n has length 2, and for every j with 0 <= j < n, 0 <= r[j][1] <= j.
preconditions: Let n = len(people). Assume: 1 <= n <= 2000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(people[i]) = 2; writing people[i] = [h_i, k_i], 0 <= h_i <= 10^6 and 0 <= k_i < n; and there is a bijection pi : {0,...,n-1} -> {0,...,n-1} such that, setting q[j] = people[pi(j)] for 0 <= j < n, for every j the number of i with 0 <= i < j and q[i][0] >= q[j][0] equals q[j][1].

statement: reconstruct_queue(people) returns a result r such that len(r) = n, every r[j] for 0 <= j < n has length 2, and for every i,j with 0 <= i < j < n and r[i][0] = r[j][0], we have r[i][1] < r[j][1].
preconditions: Let n = len(people). Assume: 1 <= n <= 2000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(people[i]) = 2; writing people[i] = [h_i, k_i], 0 <= h_i <= 10^6 and 0 <= k_i < n; and there is a bijection pi : {0,...,n-1} -> {0,...,n-1} such that, setting q[j] = people[pi(j)] for 0 <= j < n, for every j the number of i with 0 <= i < j and q[i][0] >= q[j][0] equals q[j][1].

statement: reconstruct_queue(people) returns a result r, reconstruct_queue(people') returns a result r', and r = r' (the two result vectors have the same length and the same entries at every index).
preconditions: Let n = len(people). Assume: 1 <= n <= 2000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(people[i]) = 2; writing people[i] = [h_i, k_i], 0 <= h_i <= 10^6 and 0 <= k_i < n; and there is a bijection pi : {0,...,n-1} -> {0,...,n-1} such that, setting q[j] = people[pi(j)] for 0 <= j < n, for every j the number of i with 0 <= i < j and q[i][0] >= q[j][0] equals q[j][1]. Let people' be another slice of vectors of length n such that there is a bijection tau : {0,...,n-1} -> {0,...,n-1} with people'[i] = people[tau(i)] for every i with 0 <= i < n.
